To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Maternal stress during pediatric primary health care visits can be measured reliably, (2) Maternal stress is associated with a range of negative outcomes, (3) Maternal stress can be reduced through interventions, and (4) Interventions that target maternal stress can be implemented in primary care.
the maternal stress level is significantly associated with child health status, maternal parenting stress, and child behavioral problems.

(1) Maternal stress during pediatric primary visits is associated with maternal depressive symptoms and parenting behaviors; (2) Maternal stress is associated with child behavioral problems; (3) Maternal stress mediates the relationship between maternal depressive symptoms and child behavioral problems; and (4) Maternal stress moderates the relationship between parenting behaviors and child behavioral problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the maternal stress and the child's stress are associated with the child's health.
the effects of maternal stress on the child's development, with the effects of the child's development on the mother, and with the effects of these on each other.
the effects of stress on the body and the brain, and how these effects are mediated by the endocrine and nervous systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress experienced during the pregnancy period has an effect on the child’s development.
the main cause for stress is the fear of failure.
the most important thing that can be done for children is for parents to provide a safe, nurturing environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new measure of maternal stress, the Pediatric Primary Care Stress Measure, that is valid and reliable.
maternal stress is a significant factor in child health and development and that pediatricians should routinely screen for maternal stress and provide resources for mothers to reduce maternal stress.
maternal stress during pediatric visits can be reduced through the use of a stress management intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal stress during pediatric visits is common and can be associated with negative maternal and infant outcomes.
maternal stress is a modifiable risk factor for pediatric obesity.
we need to be more aware of how stress affects our children and how we can help them cope.
